model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 4 illustrates the mean absolute values of SDPA output before and after applying gating, across different network layers, with the stated intent to show that baseline and post-gating values are similar. The horizontal axis (X-axis) is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to 20, with major tick marks and labels at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20), indicating a linear scale representing layer depth in the model. The vertical axis (Y-axis) is labeled “Mean Absolute Value” and ranges from 0.0 to 1.6, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.2 (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, ..., 1.6), also on a linear scale. Two lines are plotted: one solid green line labeled “mean abs before gate” and one solid blue line labeled “mean abs after gate.” Both lines exhibit a generally decreasing trend from layer 0 to layer 20. At layer 0, the green line starts at approximately 1.5, while the blue line begins slightly lower, around 1.4. Both lines decline gradually, with the green line remaining consistently above the blue line across all layers. By layer 20, the green line reaches approximately 0.3, and the blue line is slightly below it, at roughly 0.25. The visual proximity of the two lines across the entire range supports the caption’s assertion that baseline and post-gating values are similar.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 4 presents two line charts side by side, both plotting the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values against layer number, with the left chart using a threshold of 1e-2 and the right chart using a threshold of 1e-3, to compare the proportion of values below these thresholds before and after applying gating. The x-axis in both charts is labeled “Layer” and spans from 0 to 20 with uniform linear spacing, marked at intervals of 5. The y-axis in both charts is labeled “Sparsity Ratio” and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. In the left chart (threshold 1e-2), the green line with circle markers represents the sparsity ratio before gating, starting at approximately 0.8 at layer 0 and decreasing to around 0.3 by layer 20; the cyan line with square markers represents the sparsity ratio after average gating, beginning near 0.1 at layer 0 and rising slightly to about 0.13 by layer 20. In the right chart (threshold 1e-3), the green line with circle markers again indicates sparsity before gating, starting near 0.9 at layer 0 and declining to approximately 0.3 by layer 20; the cyan line with square markers for sparsity after average gating begins close to 0.0 at layer 0 and increases gradually to about 0.08 by layer 20. The figure caption notes that mean absolute values before and after gating are similar, though the charts specifically visualize sparsity ratios under two different thresholds.
model_annotations.English: Figure 4 presents two line plots side by side, both illustrating the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a specified threshold as a function of network layer, with the x-axis labeled “Layer” ranging from 0 to 20 and the y-axis labeled “Sparsity Ratio” ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The left plot uses a threshold of 1e-2 and shows three lines: a solid green line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03” that starts near 0.8 and declines steadily to below 0.1; a dashed blue line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44” that begins near 0.6 and decreases to around 0.1; and a dotted red line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33” that starts near 0.7 and falls to approximately 0.1. The right plot uses a stricter threshold of 1e-3 and displays the same three line styles and colors: the green line (“sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003”) begins near 0.8 and drops to below 0.1; the blue line (“sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126”) starts near 0.4 and declines to around 0.05; and the red line (“sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.088”) begins near 0.5 and decreases to approximately 0.05. In both plots, all lines exhibit a general downward trend across layers, with the “before gate” values consistently higher than the “after gate” and “after average gate” values at most layers.
